case.title: Syrah's Mozambique-to-Louisiana anode chain
case.subtitle: Syrah Technologies LLC · Vidalia, Louisiana, USA (graphite from Balama, Mozambique)
case.question: Could Sayari trace a graphite anode chain with no Chinese owner, from mine to US plant, and show whether the same mine also feeds Chinese-owned plants?
case.answer: Yes for the mine-to-plant leg and the mine's other buyers: dated rows show Balama graphite reaching Vidalia and also going to Chinese graphite firms and BTR's Chinese-owned Indonesian plant. No for the last leg: no Vidalia sales to US buyers are visible, and ownership needed the company's own annual report.
case.why_it_matters: Under the post-July 2025 tax-credit rules, the question is who owns each supplier. Here the owners are Australian at every step, so this is what a chain that passes that test looks like on paper. But the same mine sells to Chinese-owned plants, so 'Mozambican graphite' on its own says nothing about who processed it.
case.headline: A clean chain looks almost the same as a risky one in trade data. Sayari shows Syrah's Balama mine shipping natural graphite to its Louisiana anode plant and to Chinese graphite firms and BTR's Indonesian plant. What tells them apart is ownership, and that came mostly from Syrah's annual report, not the registry.
case.summary_for_non_experts: Syrah Resources, an Australian company, mines graphite at Balama in Mozambique and turns it into battery anode material at Vidalia, Louisiana. Tesla has a contract to buy that material. In Sayari we found the mine's shipments to Vidalia, and also its shipments to eight Chinese buyers and to BTR's Chinese-owned plant in Indonesia. Vidalia itself is still at qualification scale and its US sales don't show up in customs data. So the chain is Australian-owned from start to finish, but it shares a mine with the chains this site questions.

steps.title: Who owns the chain
steps.text: Syrah's 2025 annual report says it owns 95% of Twigg, the mine company, 100% of Syrah Technologies in Vidalia and 100% of Syrah Global DMCC in Dubai. Sayari's registry data show part of this: Syrah owns an Australian holding company, and a holding company of the same name is the Vidalia company's member. Sayari has no owners for the mine, and its ownership tools returned nothing for either company.

steps.title: Mine to plant: Mozambique to Louisiana
steps.text: Seven dated rows show natural graphite (HS 2504.10, flake mined from the ground) going from Twigg at Nacala to Vidalia via New Orleans, Sep 2023 to Jan 2024. Another 26 rows of natural flake reached Vidalia through ports such as Busan, Veracruz and Shanghai, Sep 2023 to Nov 2024, with no supplier named. Their sizes match Twigg's lots, but no record says so.

steps.title: What else goes into a 'clean' plant
steps.text: Vidalia's carbonisation furnaces, mills and mixers came from Chinese makers, one of them state-owned. That is why Sayari flags the plant 'chinese_soe_adjacent'. One 20-tonne lot of Chinese spherical graphite (HS 3801.90) arrived in Oct 2023. Coating pitch came from Rain Carbon in Germany. Equipment doesn't count toward the ownership test, but it shows how hard it is to avoid China completely.

steps.title: Same mine, Chinese buyers
steps.text: The mine's 190 visible export rows go mostly to China (89) and to European refractory and graphite firms. The China rows, all in 2022, went to Qingdao graphite companies, traders and a refractory maker. Twigg also shipped flake to BTR's Chinese-owned plant in Indonesia in 2024 and 2025, and Syrah's Dubai arm sold it more in 2026. Two Qingdao buyers share names with suppliers to POSCO in Case 4.

steps.title: Where the trail goes dark: the US sale
steps.text: Sayari shows only one Vidalia export: a 50 kg lot to a Ukrainian graphite miner in Dec 2024. Sales to US buyers would be domestic and never appear in customs data. Tesla's 2021 offtake survives: Tesla withdrew a termination notice in mid-2026 but can still end the deal if final qualification fails. The plant made about 150 t for qualification in the June 2026 quarter.

caveats: Selling Mozambican graphite to Chinese buyers is legal and common. Nothing here shows wrongdoing by any company named.
Buyers are named because they appear in customs records; this says nothing about their compliance.
Twigg's Vidalia rows come from Korean transshipment data, and US import data hold rows loaded at Busan. Some may be the same cargo seen twice, so we don't add the two counts.
A port of loading (e.g. Shanghai) is not a country of origin. The Shanghai-loaded flake rows name no supplier.
All China rows we found are from 2022. Later trade may exist outside Sayari's coverage.
Plant status and the Tesla offtake come from the company and the press (Tavily), not from Sayari.
Entity-resolution links are our judgment and could be wrong.
Sayari has since filed the Aug 2025 Twigg → BTR Indonesia row under another Twigg record (pINZVxJgOaXpyrNkPgaeBQ); the shipment itself was re-confirmed on 18 Oct 2026.

calls.question: Which Sayari records describe the Vidalia anode plant?
calls.result_summary: 5 records. The main one, SYRAH TECHNOLOGIES LLC (NvC-a4BgmoxO63ubVyUiUQ), carries a Louisiana SOS ID (42632807Q), a SAM UEI and the Vidalia address 2001 D.A. Biglane Road. Two EPA facility records (the '10 KTA active anode material facility' and a 'graphite qualification facility') and a trade-only 'SYRAH TECHNOLOGIES' share that street address. A fifth is a Delaware file-number record.
calls.interpretation: One plant, several records. The address ties four of them together; the main record holds the identifiers.

calls.question: Which Sayari record is the Australian parent?
calls.result_summary: Syrah Resources Limited (ex1GaqYc9OHlM2KgDrK-5w) with LEI 254900ZS2VP83B6L6Y30, ABN 77125242284 and SEC CIK 0001639151, Melbourne addresses. Also Syrah Resources (KSA), Syrah Resources Group Holdings and three 'Syrah Resources and Trading DMCC' records in Dubai, one at '1004-B Indigo Icon'.

calls.question: Who buys from the Balama mine?
calls.result_summary: 27 buyers. US: Syrah Technologies LLC (Vidalia) and Hiller Carbon. China: Qingdao Nanshu Graphite, Qingdao Luowei New Materials, Qingdao Heshengkai Carbon Material, AW-Lin Jiangsu Supply Chain, Dinur (Yingkou) Refractory, ASK Resources. Indonesia: PT Indonesia BTR New Energy Material. Korea: POSCO Chemical (Future M), Elves Graphite, Chosun Refractories. Europe: RHI Magnesita and affiliates, Vesuvius Belgium, Grafitbergbau Kaisersberg, Dominik Georg Luh Technografit, CS Additive, ArcelorMittal Refractories and others. calls.interpretation: One mine, many chains: the US anode plant, a Chinese-owned anode plant in Indonesia, Chinese graphite processors and a long list of refractory makers.

calls.question: What arrives at the Vidalia plant, and from whom?
calls.result_summary: 73 rows, Dec 2022 – Jul 2026. Graphite: 7 rows of natural graphite (HS 2504.10) from Twigg, Nacala to New Orleans, Sep 2023 – Jan 2024 (about 2,507 t; recorded in Korean transshipment data); 26 more rows described as natural flake graphite (HS 2504.10) with no supplier named, Sep 2023 – Nov 2024 (about 9,739 t), loaded at Busan (8), Shanghai (5), Veracruz (4) and six other ports; one 20 t row of 'spherical graphite' (HS 3801.90) from Qingdao Mien New Material, Oct 2023; one 4.8 t HS 2504 row from Neuman & Esser, Dec 2022. Other inputs: petroleum pitch from Rain Carbon Germany (4 rows, Oct 2023 – Jun 2024). Equipment from China: carbonisation furnaces and parts from Jiangsu Qianjin Furnace (12 rows, Dec 2022 – Jan 2026), mills and baghouses from Zhejiang Leap Pulverization, a mixer from Shuanglong Group, valves from Mountop Group (China Metallurgical Equipment Nanjing, flagged state-owned), plus heating elements, valves and furnace parts from Shanghai with no shipper named (Nov 2025 – Jul 2026).
calls.interpretation: The graphite feed is Mozambican where a supplier is named. The plant also took one small lot of Chinese spherical graphite and much of its processing kit from China. The five Shanghai-loaded flake rows name no supplier; a port of loading is not proof of origin.

calls.question: What is the status of the Vidalia plant in 2025–2026?
calls.result_summary: A LinkedIn summary of Syrah's June 2026 quarterly says Vidalia produced 150 t for customer qualification. Kalkine gives capacity of 11,250 tpa. Manufacturing Digital (29 Jun 2026) says Tesla withdrew its termination notice once Vidalia began delivering conforming material. DFC announced a plan to take a strategic equity interest in Syrah (dfc.gov). The Kleinman Center (UPenn) notes the USITC's March 2026 negative vote on Chinese anode duties.
calls.interpretation: Vidalia is operating at qualification scale, not commercial volume. Small output fits the absence of US sales in trade data.

calls.question: What is the status of Tesla's offtake from Vidalia?
calls.result_summary: Syrah's 2025 annual report: Tesla served a default notice in July 2025 over non-conforming AAM samples; cure date extended to 1 June 2026. Reuters (31 May 2026), electrive (1 Jun 2026) and Yahoo Finance: Tesla withdrew its termination notice after accepting conforming samples, but kept the right to terminate if final qualification fails. The 2021 deal covers 8,000 t over four years. ION Analytics cites the 23 Dec 2021 stock-exchange announcement of the deal, a separate Lucid offtake (7 ktpa, Feb 2025) and a DOE loan under forbearance tied to the Tesla deal.
calls.interpretation: The Tesla link is a contract, not yet a flow of goods. It survives but depends on final qualification.
